source.original_title: 05/20/2026 - Tayler Ireland x Harry Edmonds KFS
source.display_title: 05/20/2026 - Tayler Ireland x Harry Edmonds KFS  — Lost

setter.name: Kim Forbes-Sobers
setter.evidence: I know you spoke with Kim. He gave me like a little bit of an overview.

prospect.name: Tayler Ireland
prospect.occupation: Carpenter / construction worker; started his own company two years ago and is in its second year
prospect.training_background: Essentially untrained — 'I haven't been one to really work out or been able to follow through on consistently working out'. Recently bought a 20 lb and a 35 lb kettlebell and has been doing three movements (curls, swings, halos) unguided. Previously attempted calisthenics, push-ups and pull-ups; 'nothing seems to stick'. Some hamstring stretching and lymphatic work, and sees 'a lady that stretches me out'.
prospect.medical: Lower back pain, on and off for over a year: a pinch on standing after lying down, sometimes cannot stand up directly and has to roll onto his side and get up slowly. No radiating leg pain when asked. Self-suspects anterior pelvic tilt and tight hamstrings. Physically demanding trade — 'I'm pretty bagged after work'. No clinician involved beyond a stretch practitioner.

signals: Proposed label: the_reluctant_starter — never had a training identity at all ('I've never seen myself as a person who works out. That's just been a story in my head'), is not deconditioned or in crisis, and is negotiating with his own resistance rather than with the price or the programme
Does not fit the_rebuilder (no former self to recover), the_optimizer (has never trained), or the_medically_constrained (nothing has been ruled out by a clinician)
Self-reliant to the point of it being the stated blocker: 'I'm fairly stubborn and I do everything by myself on my own... reaching out for help and stuff like that's usually a bit of an issue'
Bought the equipment before the call, which is intent — but wants the outcome to be effortless: 'I want it to be easy and just kind of roll in'

goals.text: Move more freely and feel more spry
Stop being crippled on the couch at the end of the day and get his evenings back
Build core and general strength to make his carpentry work easier
Become someone who works out — change the story that he is not that person

pains.text: Lower back pinch for over a year; sometimes cannot stand up without rolling onto his side first
Nothing sticks — goes all in, then fades out instead of showing up when it is hard
Physically drained after a day of carpentry, and not a morning person
Working out is overwhelming — too many exercises and too many right and wrong ways to do them
Second year of a new business absorbing his time and attention
Stubborn self-reliance makes asking for help difficult
Lives in his head and struggles to get into his body

objections.raw_quote: Yeah, I mean, I think I'm going to go with a no. I'm sitting here hesitating too much.
objections.rep_response: Accepted it without pushing, then asked one further diagnostic question about the nature of the resistance and gave parting advice — build a small daily habit, do 20 push-ups or deep squats — and left the door open

objections.raw_quote: like I said, I just kind of started this company, and I'm only in the second year, so there's a lot on my plate. And so I'm just worried that I, you know, struggle to make that time or find that time.
objections.rep_response: Ran the make-time-versus-find-time reframe: 'The truth is, you can't find the time. It's just, it's more making it... setting it out as a priority and drawing a line in the sand'

objections.raw_quote: I feel like I have the ability to tackle this in my own way.
objections.rep_response: Conceded the premise and reframed on difficulty: 'the truth is you can do it on your own, everyone can, everyone has the ability to but the truth that comes along with that truth is that it's harder'

offer.guarantee_mentioned: And we guarantee the results too.

evidence: Explicit no from the prospect: 'I think I'm going to go with a no. I'm sitting here hesitating too much.'
Prospect qualified it himself: 'if I was like, I gotta be a hell yes, I think'
The programme was never presented; the rep raised the price only as an illustration while explaining why he would not sell it — 'the coaching for six months is... six grand US'
Rep deliberately declined to close: 'my job is to sell you a 6k usd program right but i've got a heart to i'm not gonna hard sell you something you don't want to do'
Counter-evidence: the prospect left the door open — 'Maybe I'll come back to this' — and the rep offered to text him, so a later re-engagement is plausible
outcome.next_step: No next step booked. Rep advised building a small daily habit (20 push-ups or deep squats), suggested a self-reflection exercise, and said to get in touch if he becomes ready

notable.note: The best-run commitment gate in the batch and the strongest counterexample to the rest of the corpus. The rep asked the readiness question three times, refused to present the offer until he had a yes, got a clear no and stopped — 'I don't want you to spend any money if you're not ready.' He also ran the only genuine clinical screening question found anywhere in this batch, testing for radiating leg pain when the prospect described a lower-back pinch. Against that: he then prescribed daily push-ups and deep squats to a man with a year of on-and-off back pain and told him 'You have the capability to have no pain', with no suggestion of a clinical assessment. Also worth noting for coaching review is the pastoral turn at the end — a mentor's meditation about 'the most whole version of you' — delivered on a recorded commercial call.

quality.notes: The prospect is labelled 'Zoom user' throughout and is never named in the transcript except by the rep addressing him as 'Taylor'; the name in this record comes from the title. Long inverted run-on blocks at 00:10:58-00:12:00 and 00:19:35-00:21:00 carry the rep's speech inside the prospect's turn and vice versa. The decision moment at 00:18:09-00:18:26 is split across labels, with 'I'm going to go with a no' and 'I'm sitting here hesitating too much' landing on different speakers. An early line, 'I don't know why you sound very Muslim for a sec', appears to be corrupted ASR in an exchange about accents ('Are you English?' / 'Nope... Canadian') and has been treated as a transcription artefact rather than as speech.
